# Overview

Before any of the analysis labs will run, you need R, Quarto and an editor on your
machine, and they need to be able to find each other.

This lab is not analysis. It is plumbing. Work through it in order and do not skip
the checkpoints: each one tells you whether the previous step actually worked,
which is much cheaper than discovering it in the middle of Lab 01.

Budget about forty minutes, most of which is waiting for downloads.

# Choose your route

You can do every lab in this module with **either** of two editors. Pick one and
follow it all the way through. You do not need both.

| | **Route A — VS Code** | **Route B — RStudio** |
| :- | :- | :- |
| What it is | A general-purpose editor, plus R and Quarto extensions | An editor built specifically for R |
| Choose it if | You already use VS Code for other modules, or want one editor for everything | You are new to R, or want the least setup |
| Quarto | Installed separately (Step 2) | Comes bundled with RStudio |
| How you render | `quarto render` in the terminal, or the Render button | The **Render** button |
| Setup effort | More: the terminal must be able to find R and Quarto (Step 4) | Less: RStudio finds R by itself |

| Tool | Route A — VS Code | Route B — RStudio |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **R**, the language that does the analysis | Yes | Yes |
| **Quarto**, turns a document containing R code into a web page | Yes, standalone install | Bundled, nothing to install |
| **Editor** | VS Code + two extensions | RStudio Desktop |

The analysis labs work identically on both routes. The module's live demos use
VS Code, but nothing in a lab depends on it.

Most steps below have a **VS Code** tab and an **RStudio** tab. Click the tab for
your route once: every other tab on the page switches with it.

---

# Step 1 — Install R

**Both routes.** RStudio does not include R; it needs R installed first.

**Windows.** Download from [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org) →
*Download R for Windows* → *base* → *Download R x.x.x for Windows*. Run the
installer and accept the defaults.

**macOS.** Same site → *Download R for macOS* → the `.pkg` matching your chip
(Apple silicon or Intel).

You need **R 4.6.0 or later**. If you have an older R from a previous module,
install the new one anyway: packages are installed per R version, so you will
install them again in Step 5.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Route A, Windows: the R installer does not add R to your PATH

This is deliberate on their part and inconvenient for VS Code users. Step 4 fixes
it. Do not skip Step 4 just because the installer said it finished successfully.
RStudio users can ignore this: RStudio finds R without PATH.
:::

# Step 2 — Install Quarto

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

Download the installer for your platform from
[quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started) and run it.

On Windows you can also use:

```powershell
winget install --id Posit.Quarto
```

::: {.callout-important}
### Do not rely on a copy inside RStudio

If you also have RStudio, it ships its own private copy of Quarto at a path like
`C:\Program Files\RStudio\resources\app\bin\quarto\bin`. It is tied to your
RStudio version and moves when RStudio updates. On the VS Code route, install
Quarto properly as above.
:::

## RStudio

**Nothing to do.** RStudio includes Quarto, and its **Render** button uses that
copy. Skip to Step 3.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Optional: a standalone Quarto as well"}
The bundled copy is only visible inside RStudio. If you also want to run `quarto`
commands from a terminal, or get Quarto updates sooner than RStudio releases them,
install it from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started)
too. The labs do not need this.
:::

:::

# Step 3 — Install your editor

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

Download VS Code from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com).

Then open the Extensions panel (`Ctrl+Shift+X`, or `Cmd+Shift+X` on macOS) and
install:

| Extension | Publisher | What it gives you |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **Quarto** | Posit | Syntax highlighting for `.qmd`, a Render button, live preview |
| **R** | REditorSupport | R syntax highlighting and a console inside the editor |

## RStudio

Download **RStudio Desktop** (the free version) from
[posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop)
and run the installer. Install R first (Step 1): RStudio looks for R when it
starts.

Open RStudio. You should see four panes, one of them the **Console**, whose first
lines report the R version, for example `R version 4.6.0`.

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Windows: RStudio picked up an old R"}
If the Console reports an R older than 4.6.0, you have more than one R installed.
Go to *Tools → Global Options → General → R version*, click **Change**, choose the
4.6.x installation, then restart RStudio.
:::

:::

# Step 4 — Make your terminal find R and Quarto

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

This is the step that causes almost every problem people report on this route.
Two separate things go wrong.

### Your PATH may not include R

Open a terminal in VS Code with `` Ctrl+` `` and run:

```powershell
Rscript --version
```

If that reports a version, skip to the next heading. If it says *not recognized*,
find your R installation and add it:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\R"
```

Take the folder name it reports — something like `R-4.6.0` — and substitute it
below:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $env:Path + ";C:\Program Files\R\R-4.6.0\bin", "User")
```

### Your terminal is holding a stale copy of PATH

A terminal keeps the environment it started with, and **VS Code hands every new
terminal a cached copy**. So after installing anything, a brand new terminal panel
will still not see it.

To refresh the terminal you are in right now:

```powershell
$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
```

To fix it permanently, **close VS Code completely** — every window, not *Reload
Window* — and reopen it.

::: {.callout-note}
#### macOS and Linux

Both installers put R and Quarto on your PATH without help. If a command is not
found, close the terminal and open a new one, and if that fails, restart VS Code.
:::

## RStudio

**Nothing to do.** RStudio finds R and its own Quarto without using PATH. Skip to
Checkpoint 1.

:::

---

# Checkpoint 1 — Are the tools visible?

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

Run all three in a VS Code terminal:

```powershell
quarto --version
Rscript --version
code --version
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false" title="What you should see"}
Three version numbers. Quarto should be **1.4 or later** and R **4.6.0 or later**.

If any command is *not recognized*, go back to Step 4. Do not continue — nothing
below will work.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="PowerShell: why `R --version` fails even when R works"}
`R` is a built-in PowerShell alias for `Invoke-History`, so `R --version` never
reaches your R installation. You will see a confusing error mentioning
*"Cannot locate the history for command line"*.

Use `Rscript --version` instead, or `R.exe --version` to bypass the alias.
`Rscript` is the one that matters anyway — it is what Quarto calls.
:::

## RStudio

Type this in the RStudio **Console** and press Enter:

```r
R.version.string
```

Then check that RStudio knows about Quarto: open the *File → New File* menu.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false" title="What you should see"}
The Console prints something like `"R version 4.6.0 (2026-04-24)"`: it must be
**4.6.0 or later**.

The *New File* menu lists **Quarto Document...**. If it does not, your RStudio is
too old to include Quarto: install the current version from Step 3.
:::

:::

# Step 5 — Install the R packages

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

In a VS Code terminal:

```powershell
Rscript -e "install.packages(c('readr','dplyr','tidyr','ggplot2','knitr','rmarkdown'), repos='https://cloud.r-project.org')"
```

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="PowerShell mangles quotes — use the right ones"}
Note the quoting above: **double quotes outside, single quotes inside**. PowerShell
strips double quotes when passing arguments to a program, so the reverse
arrangement arrives at R as `install.packages(c(readr,dplyr,...), repos=https:/)` and
fails with `unexpected '/'`.
:::

## RStudio

In the RStudio **Console**:

```r
install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
```

If RStudio asks you to choose a download mirror, pick any; *0-Cloud* is fine.

:::

Those six are all the labs need: `readr` reads the CSV files, `dplyr` and `tidyr`
reshape and summarise data (from Lab 01), `ggplot2` draws the report figures from
Stage 3, and `knitr` and `rmarkdown` let Quarto run R. Installing
them all now means no lab stops halfway for a download. Accept any prompt about a
personal library.

# Step 6 — Get the project and the data

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/nmcguinness/L8-3DGD-Playtest-Analytics.git
cd L8-3DGD-Playtest-Analytics
code .
```

No Git? Use the green **Code** button on the repository page →
*Download ZIP*, then unzip it and open the folder in VS Code with *File → Open
Folder*.

## RStudio

**With Git:** *File → New Project → Version Control → Git*, paste
`https://github.com/nmcguinness/L8-3DGD-Playtest-Analytics.git` as the repository
URL, choose where to put it, and click **Create Project**.

**No Git?** Use the green **Code** button on the repository page →
*Download ZIP* and unzip it. Then *File → New Project → Existing Directory*, browse
to the unzipped folder, and click **Create Project**.

::: {.callout-important}
### Always work inside the project

An RStudio project sets the working directory to the project folder, which is why
paths like `data/tidebreak_sessions.csv` work. Reopen it each time with *File →
Open Project* (or the `.Rproj` file), not by opening a single `.qmd` on its own.
The project name should show in the top-right corner of RStudio.
:::

:::

The `data/` folder contains the CSVs every lab uses.

---

# Checkpoint 2 — Render something

Create a new file called `test.qmd` in the project folder, beside the `data/`
folder, with exactly this content. (RStudio: *File → New File → Quarto Document*,
choose **Create Empty Document**, paste, and save as `test.qmd`.)

```` markdown
---
title: "Setup test"
---

## Does R work?

```{{r}}
library(readr)
sessions <- read_csv("data/tidebreak_sessions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(sessions)
```

## Does plotting work?

```{{r}}
hist(sessions$score, breaks = 20, main = "Score", xlab = "Score")
```
````

Then render it:

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## VS Code

```powershell
quarto render test.qmd
```

Or open `test.qmd` and click the **Render** button at the top right of the editor.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false" title="What success looks like"}
The terminal reports `Output created: test.html`. Open that file in a browser and
you should see the number **120** and a histogram.

If you see both, everything works and you are ready for Lab 01. Delete `test.qmd`
and `test.html`.
:::

## RStudio

Open `test.qmd` and click **Render** in the toolbar above it, or press
`Ctrl+Shift+K` (`Cmd+Shift+K` on macOS).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false" title="What success looks like"}
The **Background Jobs** pane shows the render, then the result opens in the
**Viewer** pane or a browser window. You should see the number **120** and a
histogram.

If you see both, everything works and you are ready for Lab 01. Delete `test.qmd`
and `test.html`.
:::

:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="If the render fails"}
Work through these in order.

**`could not find function "read_csv"`** or **`there is no package called
'readr'`** — Step 5 did not complete. Re-run it and watch for errors.

**RStudio says `rmarkdown` or `knitr` is required** — Step 5 did not complete.
Click **Install** in the prompt, or re-run Step 5.

**`cannot open file 'data/tidebreak_sessions.csv'`** — you are not in the project
folder, or `test.qmd` is not beside the `data/` folder. VS Code: run
`Get-Location` to see where you are and `Get-ChildItem data` to confirm the CSVs
are there. RStudio: check the project name in the top-right corner, and that the
**Files** pane shows `data/` beside `test.qmd`.

**`Unable to locate an installed version of R`** (VS Code) — Quarto cannot find R.
This is Step 4. Confirm `Rscript --version` works *in the same terminal* you are
rendering from.

**No error, but nothing happens** (VS Code) — the terminal may be busy with another
process. Open a second terminal with the `+` button in the terminal panel.
:::

---

# Troubleshooting reference

Keep this. Every one of these has bitten someone on this module.

| Route | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| :- | :- | :- | :- |
| VS Code | `'quarto' is not recognized` | PATH not refreshed since install | Refresh line in Step 4, then restart VS Code fully |
| VS Code | `'Rscript' is not recognized` | Windows R installer does not set PATH | Step 4, first half |
| VS Code | `R : Cannot locate the history for command line` | `R` is a PowerShell alias for `Invoke-History` | Use `Rscript` or `R.exe` |
| VS Code | `unexpected '/' in "install.packages..."` | PowerShell stripped your double quotes | Double outside, single inside |
| VS Code | Command works in one terminal, not a new one | VS Code caches the environment per terminal | Close VS Code entirely and reopen |
| VS Code | `Unable to locate an installed version of R` | Quarto cannot see R on PATH | Step 4, then check in the *same* terminal |
| RStudio | Console reports an old R version | More than one R installed | *Tools → Global Options → General → R version* (Step 3) |
| RStudio | No **Quarto Document** in *File → New File* | RStudio too old to include Quarto | Install the current RStudio (Step 3) |
| RStudio | `cannot open file 'data/...'` | Working outside the RStudio project | *File → Open Project* (Step 6) |
| Both | Render works, but a plot is missing | The chunk is `{r}` with a typo, or the code errored above it | Read the render output from the top; the first error is the real one |
| Both | `Error in library(x) : there is no package called 'x'` | Package not installed for *this* R version | Re-run Step 5; check the R version matches the one you installed |

---

# What to do if you are still stuck

Post in the module forum with **all three** of the following, or nobody can help
you:

1. Your route (VS Code or RStudio) and the exact command you ran or button you
   clicked
2. The complete error message, copied as text rather than a screenshot
3. Your versions: VS Code users, the output of `quarto --version` and
   `Rscript --version`; RStudio users, the output of `R.version.string` and the
   RStudio version from *Help → About RStudio*

The third one resolves about half of these on its own.
